headline: Jamaat leader Akhtaruzzaman placed on 1-day remand over airport disorder
summary: The former MP is accused of assaulting a security supervisor and threatening airport officials following delays in luggage and Zamzam water distribution.
details: A Dhaka court has granted police one day of remand for Jamaat-e-Islami leader Mohammad Akhtaruzzaman Ranjan. He is accused of creating disorder and assaulting a security supervisor at Shahjalal International Airport.
caption:
A former MP and Jamaat leader is in police custody after a heated confrontation at the airport.

A Dhaka court has granted police one day of remand for Jamaat-e-Islami leader Mohammad Akhtaruzzaman Ranjan. He is accused of creating disorder and assaulting a security supervisor at Shahjalal International Airport.

headline_marked: 7 killed in Mymensingh road crash; [[bus driver sued for reckless driving]]
headline: 7 killed in Mymensingh road crash; bus driver sued for reckless driving
summary: A Rajib Paribahan bus collided with a CNG-powered auto-rickshaw on the Mymensingh-Jamalpur highway, killing seven people including three women and a child.
details: A Rajib Paribahan bus traveling from Dhaka to Jamalpur collided with a CNG-powered auto-rickshaw on the Akua bypass road of the Mymensingh-Jamalpur regional highway yesterday.

All seven people in the auto-rickshaw were killed at the scene. The victims include Mofazzal Hossain Lebu (50), his mother Rashida Begum (70), his daughter Marjina Begum (25), and Marjina's five-year-old son Minal.
Also killed were Akram Ali (51), his wife Momota Begum (39), and the auto-rickshaw driver Sujon Ali (42).
A case has been filed against the bus driver at Mymensingh Kotwali Model Police Station, alleging reckless and speeding driving.
The bus driver and helper fled the scene immediately after the collision. Police have seized both the bus and the auto-rickshaw.
The bodies were handed over to the families without autopsies following legal procedures, and the victims were buried in their family cemeteries in Jamalpur.
caption:
Seven lives lost in an instant. A child, three women, and three men were killed when a speeding bus hit an auto-rickshaw in Mymensingh.

A Rajib Paribahan bus traveling from Dhaka to Jamalpur collided with a CNG-powered auto-rickshaw on the Akua bypass road of the Mymensingh-Jamalpur regional highway yesterday.

All seven people in the auto-rickshaw were killed at the scene. The victims include Mofazzal Hossain Lebu (50), his mother Rashida Begum (70), his daughter Marjina Begum (25), and Marjina's five-year-old son Minal.

Also killed were Akram Ali (51), his wife Momota Begum (39), and the auto-rickshaw driver Sujon Ali (42).

A case has been filed against the bus driver at Mymensingh Kotwali Model Police Station, alleging reckless and speeding driving.

The bus driver and helper fled the scene immediately after the collision. Police have seized both the bus and the auto-rickshaw.

The bodies were handed over to the families without autopsies following legal procedures, and the victims were buried in their family cemeteries in Jamalpur.

#Bangladesh #Mymensingh #RoadSafety #Accident #Justice
